conviction_note: Q4 adjusted EBITDA is arithmetically pinned near $166m by the company's own numbers (Q1 $167m + Q2 $179m + Q3 $183m = $529m against a $685-705m FY guide, and management's statement that H2 was originally guided at $350m with Q3 landing $183m), so the whole reaction sits on the FY27 guide; the three incremental things I found - a near-empty diesel hedge book into record diesel, a soft read from UNFI's most concentrated public customer, and a first-print CFO amid five C-suite changes in seven weeks - all lean the same way as the +6.97 put skew and the -6.65% 20-day run-in, so most of it is already in the price and I claim only about a fifth of the 12.5% implied move.

findings.finding: UNFI's fuel hedge book is a $5m Level-2 current asset as of 2026-05-02 (up from $1m at 2026-01-31) - trivially small against a $1.87/gal year-over-year diesel move - and being entirely current it expires inside FY27, exactly the year whose guide is set on 8 September, with US on-highway diesel at $5.599/gal on 2026-08-31 (+$1.865 YoY) after having fallen to $4.578 on 2026-07-06.
findings.why_not_priced: On the 9 June call management named 'fuel hedging' first of three mitigation levers when pressed on fuel by R5 Capital, and that framing is what the market is working from; the 10-Q fair-value table shows the hedge is a $5m current asset, i.e. immaterial and expiring, and the DERIVATIVES note itself lists only interest-rate swaps so a reader of the note alone would never see the fuel book at all. If the market had read this, a preview would describe the hedge as de minimis rather than as a mitigant, and the two-estimate FY27 consensus would carry an explicit fuel line. The separate and larger point the price cannot yet hold is the path: diesel fell to $4.578 in early July, making the fuel scare look resolved, then re-spiked to a record, so the fuel curve against which the FY27 guide must be set is materially worse than the one visible when management last spoke. I am discounting heavily because the -4.08% five-day run-in overlaps the week diesel set its record, which is evidence the market is pricing some of this.
findings.independence: Two independent non-SEC sources point the same way: the EIA weekly retail diesel series (https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=pet&s=emd_epd2d_pte_nus_dpg&f=W, showing $3.897 on 2026-03-02 rising to $5.401, $5.640 through May, $4.578 on 2026-07-06 and $5.652 on 2026-08-24) and Fortune's 2026-09-04 report of a record $5.85/gal explicitly tied to grocery supply chains (https://fortune.com/2026/09/04/diesel-record-price-groceries/). Note the 'higher freight costs' line in finding 2 corroborates this same cost thesis - treat the two as partially overlapping, not additive.

findings.finding: Natural Grocers by Vitamin Cottage, which buys 69% of its product from UNFI, reported its quarter ended 2026-06-30 - sitting entirely inside UNFI's Q4 - with net sales up only 1.8%, daily average transaction COUNT down 1.8%, gross margin down 60bp on unfavourable mix and higher freight, and cut the top end of both its FY26 EPS guide ($2.15 to $2.11) and its comp guide (2.5% to 2.0%), all against a prior-year base that its own release says was distorted by the cybersecurity incident at its primary distributor.
findings.why_not_priced: NGVC's release never names UNFI, and nothing bridges a small natural-foods retailer's 8-K to a $2.7bn wholesaler's Q4 - UNFI carries two published estimates, so there is no mechanism by which such a read-through gets marked. If it were priced you would see UNFI's natural-segment growth expectation publicly stepped down from the +4.4% posted in Q3, and there is no revision note doing that. The specific unpriced content is the direction of units: NGVC grew dollars 1.8% while shrinking traffic 1.8% against a comp depressed by UNFI's own June-2025 outage, which implies natural-channel case volume in UNFI's Q4 was weaker than the Q3 exit rate rather than stronger.
findings.independence: Amazon's Q2 2026 supplemental shows Physical Stores (predominantly Whole Foods, UNFI's largest customer) at $5,794m vs $5,595m, +4% - steady rather than accelerating, so it neither confirms nor contradicts, and it is the reason my band crosses zero: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1018724/000101872426000024/amzn-20260630xex991.htm. The freight-cost element of this finding shares a cost driver with finding 1 and should not be counted twice.

findings.finding: Five senior officer changes between 2026-07-09 and 2026-08-24 - CFO Matteo Tarditi moved to President/COO, Louis Martin to Chief Commercial Officer, external hire Alfredo Luchini (ex-Carrier) became CFO on 2026-08-10, Chief Supply Chain Officer Mark Bushway exits 2027-01-01, and Chief Corporate Affairs Officer Matthew Echols ceased to serve on 2026-08-24 - so a CFO four weeks into the seat delivers UNFI's first multi-year guide, and the Echols departure was disclosed only in an exit Form 4 with no 8-K and no press release.
findings.why_not_priced: The Echols exit exists only as a Form 4 with no transactions and a single footnote, filed 2026-08-27 - there is no press release and no 8-K item 5.02 for it, so no news aggregator, no Zacks note and no wire preview carries it, and the count of C-suite changes is therefore understated everywhere the market looks. On the guide itself: with two published FY27 estimates there is no consensus number visible against which a conservative first guide could already be marked, so 'new CFO resets the base' cannot be in the price the way it would be on a twenty-analyst name, where you would see a pre-print estimate cut cluster. What holds this finding down, and why the band crosses zero, is that the print was pulled forward roughly three weeks from the late-September/early-October date UNFI used in each of the prior three years (last year's Q4 release was 2025-09-30), landing 38 days after fiscal year end - reporting early with a month-old CFO argues for a clean, confident close rather than a reset.
findings.independence: A second, separate SEC document: the exit Form 4 for Matthew T Echols, period 2026-08-24, filed 2026-08-27 - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000162828026059263/0001628280-26-059263-index.htm. This is a different filing from the July 8-K but the same theme, so the two should collapse to one source cluster.

searched_and_found_nothing: Whole Foods / Amazon primary distribution agreement - runs to May 2032 after the May 2024 eight-year extension, no near-term renewal risk and nothing new since (https://www.unfi.com/news-and-resources/articles/news/unfi-contract-renewal-whole-foods-market.html)

Retail-segment divestiture: no assets-held-for-sale line on the 2026-05-02 balance sheet (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1020859/000102085926000015/R2.htm), and the only retail action since is three Cub stores sold to franchisee Jerry's Enterprises on 2026-08-17, terms undisclosed and immaterial (https://www.grocerydive.com/news/unfi-selling-cub-foods-stores-jerrys-minneapolis-grocery-supermarkets/828011/)
Activist or strategic-review stake - the only ownership filing since June is a routine Vanguard Capital Management Schedule 13G filed 2026-07-31

New WARN filings / unannounced DC closures after the Q3 print - the only 2026 action is Sturtevant WI (443 jobs, WARN filed 2026-03-16, separations completed by mid-August), announced before the Q3 print and therefore priced

Labour disruption into the print - the one 2026 dispute (Teamsters Local 769, Pompano Beach, ~200 workers) was settled with a five-year contract ratified 2026-04-17; teamster.org shows no UNFI item in July, August or September 2026
Cyber-incident insurance recovery as a hidden FY26 EBITDA item - the $26m of direct FY25 costs were already added back in the FY25 reconciliation, so any recovery is immaterial against a $695m base

Term-loan repricing as a finding - Amendment No. 5 of 2026-06-18 cut the margin on ~$371m from SOFR+4.75% to SOFR+4.00%, roughly $2.8m a year, too small to matter (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001020859/000102085926000017/unfi-20260618.htm)
Food-at-home CPI as a revenue tailwind - +2.7% YoY in July 2026 and flat month-on-month, i.e. consistent with the 'low single-digit inflation' UNFI already guides to, no surprise either way

Quantifying UNFI's annual diesel gallons - Item 7A of the FY2025 10-K would not render through any fetch path I tried, so the fuel exposure in finding 1 is sized off the hedge asset's fair value rather than off consumption

A non-obvious upside catalyst - no source anywhere points to a first buyback authorisation or a raise to the December 2025 Investor Day targets (~$33bn sales, ~$800m adjusted EBITDA, ~$300m FCF for FY28), and that release explicitly directs cash to network, capabilities and balance sheet instead
baseline_tension: Every one of my three findings leans the same direction as the +6.97-point put skew and the -6.65% twenty-day run-in, which is precisely the configuration that means a finding is mostly priced already - the five-day slide of -4.08% overlaps the week diesel set its all-time record, so the tape has been marking the biggest of them in real time; against that, the Q4 EBITDA line is arithmetically pinned near $166m by management's own H2 framing and last year's Q4 print rose 18.45% on an outright miss because the guide and the balance sheet carried it, so I am claiming only a small residual rather than the full congruent move.
